input.title: BUG: setitem with a 0-d ndarray key raises in iloc/loc
input.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.

### Reproducible Example

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

key = np.array(1)

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [4, 5, 6]}, dtype="Int64")
df.iloc[key] = 9
# TypeError: len() of unsized object
df.iloc[key, 0] = 9
# TypeError: len() of unsized object

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [4.0, 5.0, 6.0]})
df.iloc[key] = 9
# TypeError: len() of unsized object

df = pd.DataFrame(
    {"a": pd.date_range("2000", periods=3), "b": pd.date_range("2001", periods=3)}
)
df.iloc[key, [0, 1]] = pd.Timestamp("2010")
# ValueError: Cross index must be 1 dimensional
df.loc[key] = pd.Timestamp("2010")
# InvalidIndexError: 1
```

### Issue Description

Setting with a 0-d ndarray key raises on these paths, while the same key works for getitem (GH-21946) and for setitem on a single-dtype numpy frame or a Series.

### Expected Behavior

A 0-d ndarray key behaves like the scalar it holds, e.g. `df.iloc[np.array(1)] = 9` is the same as `df.iloc[1] = 9`. Calling `lib.item_from_zerodim` on the key (and on each entry of a tuple key) at the top of `_LocationIndexer.__setitem__` fixes all of the above, as `_getitem_axis` already does for getitem.

AI disclosure: found and reduced with Claude Code (`claude opus 5.5`).
